text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH - multiple runtime pods OOMs in tokenization service (cluster: prod-us-west). Alerting oncall.

maya: just seeing the alerts, tokenizer pods (tokenizer-v2) killed on 3 nodes, CPU OOM in python preproc step. stack trace shows spike during batch pre-tokenize.

oncall-bot: paging @oncall (sam) — severity P1. Incident channel created.

sam: acknowledged. I'm paged, hopping in. Initial ask: how many pods, which nodes, any customer 5xxs?

emily: logs show kubelet evicted processes, pods terminated with OOMKilled. Nodes: ip-10-1-8-34, ip-10-1-9-12, ip-10-1-11-7. Pod count ~ 9 affected across deployment.

maya: also seeing occasional CUDA errors on the same timeframe from inference pods but majority are tokenizer CPU OOMs. Might be request amplification hitting preproc CPU.

sam: who pushed tokenizer change last 24h?

josh: rollout token-pipeline-3.5 this morning at 03:12 UTC (small batching tweak). No infra change.

alex: customer-impact: support metrics show spike in 502/503 from our proxy for ~5m window starting 1799900008. Estimated 1.2k requests impacted, some high-value customers reported timeouts.

support-bot: Notifying 3 customers on watchlist: acme-inc, fintechx, docflow.

maya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle incoming requests to tokenizer service to reduce concurrency; 2) disable pre-tokenization CPU-heavy path via feature flag; 3) cordon/fluid drain the flapping nodes if they keep evicting.

sam: execute throttle first. How do we change rate-limiter quickly?

josh: we can patch the configmap used by envoy rate-limiter config and reload via rollout. Patch: 

```bash
kubectl -n redwood patch configmap tokenizer-rate --patch '{"data":{"max_concurrency":"200"}}'
kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deployment/token-proxy
```

sam: doing the patch now. Patching and restarting token-proxy (this will cause short warmups).

(2m later)

josh: patched, rollout started. proxy pods re-created.

emily: observed request concurrency drop from ~1800 to ~220 within 30s. Tokenizer CPU utilization dropping on most nodes.

maya: good. next: flip feature flag to use lightweight tokenization path (disable pre-tokenize batching). Command: 

```bash
# feature flag toggle (internal admin API)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://admin.internal/features/tokenizer_prebatch -d '{"enabled":false}'
```

sam: feature flag call returned 200. Confirming rollout to all tokenizers via health checks.

alex: customer 5xxs trending down, back to baseline after ~4m post-throttle. Still seeing 2 pods restart loops on node ip-10-1-11-7.

emily: gathering kubelet logs for that node. There's a kernel OOM killer log mentioning process 'python3' memory spike then container OOM. Suspect memory leak triggered by specific long prompts.

maya: can we identify offending request patterns? Any large prompts or json payloads?

josh: sampling request traces from tracing store — a few requests with massive prompt repetition ( >100k tokens) from internal integration tests hitting prod accidentally. Hashes: 7f1a..., 2c3d...

sam: if that's true we should block those client keys and ban IPs temporarily. Alex, can support blacklist them?

alex: support team applied temporary API key suspend for the two keys and added IP block. Blocking took effect at 1799900090.

(another 60s)

emily: node ip-10-1-11-7 still flapping. I'm cordoning it and evicting remaining pods to test stability.

```bash
kubectl cordon ip-10-1-11-7
kubectl drain ip-10-1-11-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

sam: cordoned and drained. Monitoring.

maya: after throttle + flag + key blocks + cordon, OOMs stopped. All tokenizer pods stable, CPU normalized. CUDA errors were downstream from retry storms earlier, look resolved.

support-bot: customer updates: sent initial notification to affected customers at 1799900125. "We experienced elevated errors due to unexpected large prompt traffic, mitigations applied, services restored."

josh: rolling back token-pipeline-3.5 isn't necessary now, but we'll leave the prebatch off until we validate memory regression.

sam: quick impact summary for postmortem: root cause = unbounded large-prompt requests amplified by pre-tokenize batching change + insufficient upstream rate limits. Consequences = CPU OOM on tokenizer pods, ~1.2k 5xxs for ~5m, 3 nodes evicted, 2 customers reported.

maya: next actions (short): 1) set stricter global request size limits (enforced at edge) 2) add per-key hard token limits + circuit breaker 3) add memory guard in tokenizer and reject >X tokens early 4) run memload tests against tokenizer with large prompts 5) postmortem doc.

alex: agreed. I'll coordinate customer follow-ups and ensure SLA ticket created.

support-bot: SLA incident ticket #INC-2026-447 created and linked.

sam: handing off to on-call for the next shift. I'll stay on until postmortem draft. If anything flares, ping me.

maya: thanks team. Adding timeline to the incident doc and will own the follow-up action items.

ops-bot: incident resolved. Final status: mitigations applied, service stable. Will sync in 1h for runbook updates. :white_check_mark:

josh: quick note: pushing memo to #eng-runtime about avoiding prebatching without mem-safety tests.

maya: filing postmortem: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3210 (draft).

sam: closing incident channel in 30m unless new alerts. Good job everyone.
